Ed Skoviak Computing (ESC) is an advisory practice, dedicated to helping companies establish or further an Enterprise Architecture practice with an emphasis on helping our clients successfully integrate AI into their enterprise while maintaining architectural coherence and delivering measurable business value.

We believe that an Architecture practice is most successful when it is built organically within the company's ethos. This means that our practitioners partner with your senior IT staff and business SMEs to find and coach individuals within your existing organization to create the basis of your Enterprise Architecture Center of Excellence (CoE).

We are also available to assist existing Enterprise Architecture groups mature by examining your organization and recommending specific adjustments to your practice to increase efficiency.

Our success is measured not by the completeness of documentation, but by the business outcomes our clients achieve: reduced time-to-market, improved operational efficiency, successful technology integrations, and confident decision-making at all organizational levels.

Whether you have an existing practice or are starting a new team, we can also guide your team to higher maturity by mentoring your team into building an effective Enterprise Reference Architecture.

ESC defines Enterprise Architecture as the holistic view of the Information Technology (IT) stack in a company and the business processes that it supports. Our approach uses a focus on four architectural aspects of the firm's unique IT infrastructure: Business, Data, Application, and Technology (BDAT). We emphasize measurable business outcomes and stakeholder communication over documentation completeness. What this means is that we apply the rigor of BDAT to the existing expertise in your firm to deliver (or enhance) an Architecture CoE (practice). Each of these four aspects examined in detail by clicking on the buttons at the top of the page.

This approach is less focused on titles (Business Architect, Enterprise Architect, etc.) but rather on the practice of Architecture within a group of IT experts. We seek to leverage the IT expertise and coach the associates to work together. Our value-add is the creation of a team within the existing organization.

Some hallmarks of this practice are:

  • Measurable business outcomes tied to architectural decisions
  • Understanding Current State (baseline)
  • A comprehensive roadmap across all business units looking 3-5 years out
  • Stakeholder alignment through business-language communication
  • Rightsized documentation and governance

In many companies, the IT systems appear as a patchwork of systems. There are several causes for this (not an exhaustive list):

  • Expansion of a business capability
  • New business capability arises
  • Merger/Acquisition
  • Market Base growth
  • Addition or removal of third party tools

Too often, this expansion of IT footprint happens in a silo—especially in a firm with multiple business functions—resulting in a piecemeal Architecture. We believe the practice approach will bring order to the chaos.
